review_candidates.description: Job Summary The Senior Finance and Operations Director (SFOD) leads and directs all finance, administration, and operations functions for FHI 360’s Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) country office and its full portfolio of projects. The SFOD manages the finance, administration, and operations functions through direct reports, including direct supervision of all Finance Leads in DRC, ensuring operational priorities, compliance requirements, and service delivery expectations are completed within established goals, timelines, and organizational standards. This role partners across the Regional Hub, the HQ Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO), donors, auditors, government counterparts, and program teams to improve consistency, efficiency, compliance, and operational effectiveness in a complex, donor-funded environment. The SFOD supports execution of operational priorities within DRC and escalates broader service model, budget, or enterprise-level issues to the Country Representative and senior leadership. Responsibilities / Duties Complexity & Problem Solving: Leads financial, administrative, and operational initiatives and process improvements across the DRC country office and its projects. Translates organizational strategies, donor requirements, and operational priorities into work plans, processes, and team-level execution. Evaluates financial, administrative, and operational issues involving multiple stakeholders, systems, and delivery contexts, and determines appropriate methods and actions to support effective program delivery. Develops and manages financial, administrative, and operational processes, tools, and practices that support the country office and its projects. Identifies and addresses barriers that may affect delivery, efficiency, compliance, or service effectiveness. Uses data, stakeholder input, and professional judgment to identify trends, gaps, risks, and improvement opportunities. Key responsibilities include: Direct all finance, administration, and operations functions for the DRC country office, ensuring resources are effectively aligned with program goals and donor requirements. Directly supervise all Finance & Operations Leads in DRC, together with administration, procurement, and operations staff, setting goals, assigning work, and monitoring performance. Lead the development, execution, and monitoring of annual budgets, forecasts, pipelines, and expenditure analyses across all DRC projects. Ensure rigorous compliance with FHI 360 policies, U.S. Government regulations (including 2 CFR 200 and FAR), and DRC statutory, tax, and legal requirements. Oversee internal and external audits, ensuring findings are addressed promptly and that robust internal controls safeguard project assets and funds. Direct procurement, logistics, IT, administration, and general services, ensuring operational systems are efficient, transparent, and responsive to program needs. Design and implement operational procedures that improve cost-effectiveness, accountability, and timely service delivery across multiple project offices. Oversee financial and operational aspects of subawards, including onboarding, monitoring, compliance, reporting, and close-out. Determine resources, timelines, and priorities needed to meet country office and project-level financial and operational goals. Recommend changes to policies, procedures, and workflows affecting finance, administration, and operations in DRC. Escalate broader service model, budget, hub coordination, or enterprise-level issues to the Country Representative, Regional Hub, and senior leadership, as appropriate. Discretion & Impact: Guides execution of financial and operational plans and initiatives across the DRC country office. Makes decisions related to resources, work priorities, team execution, process implementation, and operational improvements within the latitude of established organizational policies and donor requirements. Decisions affect financial integrity, operational outcomes, service effectiveness, costs, timelines, compliance, and delivery quality across all DRC projects. Errors may affect program delivery, increase costs, delay operational outcomes, or expose the organization to compliance or reputational risk. This role contributes to short- to medium-term country office goals and supports alignment with broader regional and organizational objectives. Collaboration & Interaction: Partners with the Country Representative, Regional Hub, the HQ Office of the CFO (OCFO), donors, auditors, government counterparts, and program teams to support financial and operational alignment and effective execution. Interacts frequently with direct reports, including Finance Leads, functional peers, and cross-functional partners on matters involving multiple projects and functions. Builds relationships with key contacts inside and outside the country office to resolve issues, improve processes, and support program delivery needs. Influences adoption of consistent financial and operational practices while recognizing DRC regulatory, donor, and project-specific requirements. Represents the country office in high-level discussions with donors, auditors, partners, and government authorities on finance, operations, and compliance matters, and effectively communicates results, risks, and recommendations to leadership. Management & Supervision: Manages the finance, administration, and operations functions in DRC through direct reports, including direct supervision of all Finance Leads in DRC. Sets goals, assigns work, monitors progress, and ensures timely completion of financial and operational priorities. Provides guidance, coaching, and performance feedback to direct reports and team members. Builds team capability in financial management, operational effectiveness, service delivery, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. Guides teams in applying established policies, procedures, and donor compliance requirements while supporting continuous improvement and consistent execution. Strong understanding of how finance, administration, and operations functions support project execution across a country program and donor-funded delivery environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate financial and operational data, identify trends, and recommend practical solutions. Strong leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
